title: pack-ctl output-contract drift + dual-copy precedence (TASK-181 carry-forward)
description:
Carry-forward batch from TASK-181's gating review (light depth, 2026-08-02) plus the design question TASK-181 deliberately deferred. Three independent items, grouped because they all sit on the same pack-ctl / reconciler surface.

**Item 1 (MEDIUM, from TASK-181 review) — bin/pack-ctl.js header documents an output contract the code no longer honors.**
The header at `bin/pack-ctl.js:90-95` states: "`{ ok: true, ... }` on success (exit 0) or `{ ok: false, code, message }` on failure (exit 1; message also goes to stderr)". TASK-181 introduced a new total-failure path for `reconcile-apply` that emits `ok: false` with **exit 0** and **no** `code` and **no** `message` — it carries `planned_install_count` / `installed_count` / `source_root` instead. A consumer scripting against the documented contract will mis-parse precisely the failure mode TASK-181's AC6 existed to surface, which is the same class of invisibility that let the original outage survive multiple releases. Decide deliberately whether the CODE should conform to the header (emit code/message, exit non-zero) or the HEADER should document the new shape — do not just paper over one side.

**Item 2 (LOW, from TASK-181 review) — spec env-hygiene inconsistency.**
`tests/e2e/pack-ctl.spec.js:89-91`'s `runCli` deletes `CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR` but not `CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT`, while `tests/e2e/pack-ctl-consumer-source.spec.js:70-74`'s `runCli` deletes both. Harmless today — the one test relying on resolution order uses the verbatim `HIVEMIND_OWNED_SOURCE_ROOT` override, which outranks `CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT` — but a future test in that file depending on fallback order could flake when run inside a real plugin session where `CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT` is set in the ambient environment.

**Item 3 (design decision, deferred out of TASK-181) — dual-copy precedence for `watch`, now genuinely live.**
This was TASK-181's ORIGINAL scope. It was voided at re-scope time because the premise was false: the project-scope copy was unreachable for consumers, so two copies could never disagree. TASK-181 fixed exactly that, so the premise is now TRUE and the question is live for the first time.

A consumer can now hold `.claude/skills/watch/` (loads as `/watch`, installed via `pack-ctl reconcile-apply`, pinned by `integrations.lock.json`) AND receive the plugin's `skills/watch/` (loads as `/hivemind:watch`, advances with the plugin version). They are byte-identical today. They diverge on the next release that re-pins `watch`: the plugin copy moves, the project copy stays frozen until someone re-runs reconcile. Two near-identically-named skills at different versions of pinned third-party code, with no rule saying which is authoritative.

Note why the obvious fix is wrong: simply dropping the pack resource makes the reconciler compute a REMOVE op against every project whose lockfile already owns `skill:watch`, deleting a working skill out from under existing consumers. TASK-180 avoided this deliberately. Any solution must handle already-installed projects, not just new ones.

Relevant new fact from TASK-181: owned copies are now a SEARCH PATH, not one directory — `src/pack-apply.js#applyPlan` builds `[...new Set([sourceRoot, ...(sourceRoots || [])])]` where `sourceRoot` defaults to `<root>/assimilated-skills` and the plugin root arrives via `sourceRoots`. So the consumer's own staging dir already LEADS the plugin, per-resource, via first-existing-match in `executeInstall`. That is a de-facto precedence rule that is implemented but nowhere documented, and it may or may not be the rule we want. Candidate directions (decide, do not assume): (a) teach the reconciler to skip or actively retire a project-scope resource when the plugin ships the same id at an equal-or-newer pin, releasing the lockfile edge cleanly; (b) keep both channels, document the precedence that already exists, and give consumers a way to see which copy is active and at what pin; (c) make plugin-root shipping the only channel with a one-time migration that retires the project copy without a bare REMOVE.

Item 3 needs a human call on direction before implementation — investigate, propose, then implement the chosen option.
acceptance_criteria: Item 1: a deliberate decision is recorded (in the closing comment) on whether bin/pack-ctl.js's code conforms to its documented output contract or the header is updated to document the new reconcile-apply shape. Whichever way it goes, the header and the actual emitted shape agree, and a spec asserts the agreement so the two cannot drift again.

Item 1: if the decision is to change the exit code or add code/message, verify no existing caller or spec depends on the current exit-0 behavior before changing it — TASK-181's AC6 spec asserts the ok:false shape and must be updated in step, not broken.

Item 2: tests/e2e/pack-ctl.spec.js's runCli mirrors the env hygiene of tests/e2e/pack-ctl-consumer-source.spec.js:70-74 (deletes CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT as well as CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR), so no test in that file can be influenced by an ambient plugin-session environment.

Item 3: the precedence rule between a plugin-root-shipped resource and the same resource installed project-scope via integrations.lock.json is decided by the human and recorded in writing (docs/design/addon-packs.md or the pack-descriptor docs), including which copy is authoritative when the pins differ, and whether the de-facto search-path precedence introduced by TASK-181 is the intended rule or an accident to be changed.

Item 3: the chosen behavior is implemented and covered by specs INCLUDING the already-installed-project case — a lockfile that already owns skill:watch must NOT be left with a dangling edge and must NOT silently lose a working skill (a bare REMOVE op against existing consumers is a defect, not a solution).

Item 3: a regression spec proves the divergence scenario end to end — plugin ships watch at pin B while a project lockfile owns watch at older pin A — asserting the documented precedence actually holds.
Item 3: /hivemind:design-pack and any reconcile-facing docs state what a consumer should expect when both copies are present, and how to tell which is active and at what pin.

npm run test:all is green; no existing pack/reconcile/assimilate/apply spec regresses; dist/pack-ctl.cjs rebuilt via npm run build:plugin and committed if bundled source changes, with tests/e2e/dist-parity.spec.js passing.

comments.author: orchestrator
comments.body:
SCOPE CHANGE after the 2026-08-02 deep review (both passes, 31 confirmed findings total).

**Item 1 (pack-ctl header output contract) MOVES to TASK-183.** The deep review escalated it — pass 2 rated it HIGH — and, more importantly, it is the same code path as TASK-183's `ok`/`installed_count` predicate work. Fixing them in two tickets would mean two passes over `bin/pack-ctl.js`'s reconcile-apply branch and two `dist/pack-ctl.cjs` rebuilds. TASK-183 AC6 carries it, including the new requirement that a spec assert `result.status` and not just `json.ok` (the current spec asserts only the latter, which is why the exit-code gap shipped).

**Item 2 (spec env hygiene, `runCli` not deleting `CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT`) STAYS here.** Note it is now adjacent to TASK-183's rework of `tests/e2e/pack-ctl-consumer-source.spec.js` — sequence after TASK-183 to avoid a collision on the same spec files.

**Item 3 (dual-copy precedence) STAYS here, and the deep review gave it teeth.** It is no longer a purely hypothetical design question: pass 1 proved that the current de-facto rule (local staging dir always leads, selected by a bare `existsSync`) lets an EMPTY `assimilated-skills/<id>/` shadow the plugin's valid copy, materialize an empty skill, and record the empty-tree SHA-256 as a verified integrity at the upstream pin. TASK-183 fixes the validation hole; it does NOT decide the precedence policy. This ticket still owns that decision, and should now be decided with the empty/partial-copy case as a first-class input rather than as a clean two-valid-copies thought experiment.

Additional confirmed findings from the deep review that belong to neither TASK-183 nor TASK-185 and are folded in here as LOW: `src/mcp-server.js` line ~169 comment cites `tests/e2e/mcp-server.spec.js` as justification for exporting `recordTaskGraphNode`, but the actual lock lives in `tests/e2e/mcp-close-task.spec.js` — the comment misdirects anyone auditing the export. And `HIVEMIND_OWNED_SOURCE_ROOT` is documented as an explicit override yet is outranked by `<repoRoot>/assimilated-skills` in the full `applyPlan` pipeline (it wins inside `resolveOwnedSourceRoot`, then loses because `sourceRoot` leads `searchPath`) — decide whether the documentation or the ordering is wrong.

**Item 3 verified STILL REAL — and now sharper than when it was written.** No precedence-policy document exists anywhere. comments.author: orchestrator
comments.body:
**HUMAN DECISION RECORDED (AC4) — Item 3 direction is (a): the plugin copy wins when it is current.**

The human chose option (a) from the three candidates in the description.

**The rule:** the reconciler retires the project-scope resource when the plugin ships the same resource id at an **equal-or-newer pin**, releasing the lockfile edge cleanly. The project-scope copy survives **only when it is ahead** of the plugin — i.e. when a consumer has deliberately pinned something newer than what the plugin ships.

**Why this over the alternatives.** Option (b) would have documented the ambiguity rather than resolved it, leaving two similarly-named skills (`/watch` and `/hivemind:watch`) at different versions indefinitely. Option (c) would have removed a consumer's ability to pin a third-party skill independently of the plugin — which is the entire point of the assimilate + `integrations.lock.json` machinery, so it fights the design. Option (a) preserves independent pinning for the case that actually needs it while eliminating the confusing steady state.

**This also settles the de-facto rule TASK-181 created.** `src/pack-apply.js#applyPlan`'s search-path precedence (consumer staging dir leads the plugin, per-resource, by first-existing-match) is **an accident, not the intended rule** — it makes a *stale* project copy silently shadow a *newer* plugin copy, which is the exact inversion of the decision above. It must be reconciled with the chosen rule, not merely documented.

**Two constraints on implementation:**

1. **A bare `REMOVE` against already-installed consumers is a defect, not a solution** (AC5). TASK-180 avoided this deliberately. Retiring must release the lockfile edge without deleting a working skill out from under a project.
2. **The retire is user-visible and must be announced, never silent.** A consumer's `/watch` becomes `/hivemind:watch` — muscle memory breaks, and any script or doc referencing the old name breaks with it. Whatever surfaces the change (reconcile output, a migration note) must say so plainly.

## An unresolved wrinkle the direction does not settle — decide it as part of implementation

**"Equal-or-newer pin" may not be computable.** The `watch` pin is a git sha from assimilation, and **content hashes have no natural ordering** — given plugin pin `B` and project pin `A`, no arithmetic says which is newer.

So the rule needs a decidable comparison. Candidates, none assumed:
- **Equality only:** retire when the pins are *identical* (provably redundant copy), keep both and surface when they differ. Safe and always computable, but leaves the divergence case unresolved — which is the case AC6 exists to test.
- **An orderable version field** alongside the sha in the descriptor/lockfile, with the sha retained for integrity. Makes "newer" meaningful, at the cost of a schema addition and a migration for existing lockfiles.
- **Provenance-based:** resolve ordering from the assimilation record (when each pin was adopted) rather than from the pin itself.

**Whichever is chosen, the residual must be stated:** what happens when the comparison genuinely cannot be made. Per this repo's Empty-result contract, "cannot determine which is newer" must be distinguishable from "they are the same" — and must not silently resolve to retiring a consumer's copy.

All three delivered. **Item 5 (the TASK-181 inversion) genuinely reconciled, not paralleled** — `effectiveSourceRoots` removes exactly the `projectSourceRoot` entry, only when retiring. `HIVEMIND_OWNED_SOURCE_ROOT` arrives via `sourceRoots`, so an explicit override survives the exclusion.

**MEDIUM-1 — direction (a) is production-inert for every reachable resource.** Delivered behaviour for the motivating case is materially option (b) with a decidable escape hatch no real data uses. Needs explicit human ratification at close, or a follow-up giving `watch` an orderable pin. Until then `/watch` vs `/hivemind:watch` divergence stays an indefinite manual-review event.

**MEDIUM-2 — `bin/pack-ctl.js:461-471`'s `ok`/`failureKind` predicate is blind to the replace bucket this ticket just made executable.** `planned_install_count`/`installed_count` count only `plan.install`. Scenario: lock owns `skill:watch` at 1.0.0, plugin ships 2.0.0, plugin's owned copy missing → replace fires, `executeInstall` throws soft, entry lands in `packs[].report`, run reports `ok: true` exit 0. Same "triage numbers say fine, truth buried in the report" class TASK-181/183 closed for installs. Successful replaces are likewise invisible to the counts `commands/design-pack.md` Step 4 says to read first.

**MEDIUM-3 — owner-edge clobber, newly reachable via replace; latent, not live.** `src/pack-apply.js:437-456` sets `owners: []` then re-adds, dropping a sibling pack's edge. Verified not live (no multi-owner entries; the two built-in packs' resources are disjoint; per-pack `reconcilePack` re-plans against a fresh lock) — but this ticket moved it from the unusual staged-not-live path onto the routine live replace path, and a dropped edge transitively breaks `executeRemove`'s "still-owned resource is never deleted" guarantee.

**LOW:** (1) `:580-590` the replace bucket reports `retired: true` from plan-time `op.from`/`op.to` rather than the callee's returned metadata — a stale plan could announce a retire that didn't happen; unreachable via `reconcilePack`, but the `applyPlan` API permits it. (2) `:391-403` framework-repo edge where the search path collapses to one entry produces an empty candidates list in the error — fail-safe (throw precedes `rmSync`) but ambiguous-empty. (3) `:434-435` "no window in which the skill is absent" isn't literally true at the fs level — the pre-existing TASK-120 `rmSync`→`cpSync` window applies; interruption self-heals on the next reconcile. (4) Test budget clean, all 12 new tests encode ACs or the residual contract.

**Direct answer — for `watch` today, plugin pin B vs lock pin A (both shas): nothing is retired.** `plan()` emits a replace op, `applyPlan` computes `'undecidable'`, the project copy is kept byte-for-byte (lock pin stays A, live dir untouched, throw-free), and a non-blocking `executed: false` report entry says the drift "cannot be ordered … review manually." The consumer keeps `/watch` at pin A and `/hivemind:watch` at the plugin's — the steady state the ticket was opened to eliminate, now surfaced rather than resolved. The docs say exactly this.

comments.body:
APPROVED and closed on a green FULL-depth review. **0 HIGH / 3 MEDIUM / 4 LOW.** Commit `f503bd9`. ACs 1-2 were struck (delivered by TASK-183); AC3 and AC4-AC7 delivered here.

## AC4 — the human's decision, and what was actually delivered

**Decision (a): the plugin copy wins when it is current.** The reconciler retires the project-scope resource when the plugin ships the same id at an equal-or-newer pin; the project copy survives only when ahead. Options (b) and (c) were rejected — (b) documents the ambiguity rather than resolving it, (c) removes independent pinning, which is the point of the assimilate + lockfile machinery.

**This also settled TASK-181's search-path precedence as an ACCIDENT, not the rule.** It let a stale project copy shadow a newer plugin copy — the inversion of the decision. `effectiveSourceRoots` genuinely reconciles it rather than adding a parallel path: it removes exactly the `projectSourceRoot` entry, and only when retiring. An explicit `HIVEMIND_OWNED_SOURCE_ROOT` override arrives via `sourceRoots` and survives the exclusion.

## The finding that matters most: the rule is production-inert today

The pin comparison is decidable **only when both pins parse as exact semver**. Verified independently by the Orchestrator and confirmed by the reviewer on every leg:

- `src/pack-reconcile.js:183-190` plans **`kind: "skill"` only**; every other kind is report-only.
- The only skill-kind resources are `watch` (pin `83da59fa…`) and `ui-ux-pro-max` (pin `12b486b2…`) — **both git shas**.
- Every semver pin (`shadcn/ui` 4.13.0, `shadcn-vue` 2.7.4, `firecrawl` 3.22.3, `playwright` 0.0.77, `21st-dev-magic` 1.9.0) sits on `kind: "mcp"` — structurally unplannable.

**So for 100% of resources this code can act on, the outcome is `'undecidable'` → keep-both-and-surface. The decidable "plugin wins" branch is exercised only by fixtures.**

**Why this still closes rather than blocking.** The decision comment pre-authorized precisely this residual: it named the content-hash wrinkle (*"hashes have no natural ordering"*), listed candidates *"none assumed"*, and mandated only that the residual be stated and that *"cannot determine"* never silently retire a consumer's copy. All three delivered. Critically, **the docs do not overclaim** — `docs/design/addon-packs.md` §2.4 names `watch` as undecidable-today/kept-and-reported verbatim, and `commands/design-pack.md` Step 4 plus both SKILL copies carry the same residual. And the developer recorded the one-case-is-the-only-case fact itself at `src/pack-apply.js:144-146`, so the trade-off was informed rather than blind.

The substantive tension — the recorded reasoning rejected equality-only *because* it "leaves the divergence case unresolved," and the delivered semver rule has that same practical deficiency for all current real data — is a product/schema question, not a code defect. **Carried to the human as MEDIUM-1 rather than resolved here.**

## For `watch` today, stated plainly

Plugin ships pin B, lockfile owns pin A, both shas: **nothing is retired.** `plan()` emits a replace op, `applyPlan` computes `'undecidable'`, the project copy is kept byte-for-byte (lock pin stays A, live dir untouched, throw-free), and a non-blocking `executed: false` report entry says the drift *"cannot be ordered … review manually."* The consumer keeps `/watch` at pin A and `/hivemind:watch` at the plugin's — the steady state this ticket was opened to eliminate, now **surfaced rather than resolved**. The announcement chain was verified end to end: `applyPlan`'s report → `reconcilePack` merge (`src/pack-orchestrator.js:118`) → `bin/pack-ctl.js:442` → `packs[].report`.

## AC5 — no bare REMOVE, verified against an already-installed fixture

`applyPlan`'s `replace` bucket executes in place via `executeInstall` (materialize + update the existing lock entry), so the resource id, lock entry, and live directory are never dropped — no dangling edge. Interruption analysed: death mid-window leaves the lock at the old pin (single end-of-run commit) so the next reconcile plans an install and self-heals; death after `cpSync` before `writeLock` re-plans the replace, and the pin-gated baseline correctly skips the stale TASK-142 baseline.

## tdd discipline — both mutants killed with the export present

The captured red was `comparePinPrecedence is not a function`, an absence-of-export shape. The reviewer planted properly instead: forcing `shippedPinWins` always-true killed 3 e2e tests; forcing `comparePinPrecedence` always-`'undecidable'` killed 8 across the pure matrix and the AC6 plugin-newer and install-path tests. **Behavioural, not vacuous.**

## Follow-ups minted — MEDIUM-2 and MEDIUM-3 are NOT dropped

- **TASK-199** — `bin/pack-ctl.js:461-471`'s `ok`/`failureKind` predicate counts only `plan.install`, so a soft-failing **replace** reports `ok: true` exit 0 with the truth buried in `packs[].report`. Same class TASK-181/183 closed for installs, re-opened on the bucket this ticket just made executable.
- **TASK-200** — owner-edge clobber at `src/pack-apply.js:437-456`: `owners: []` then re-add drops a sibling pack's edge. Not live today (no multi-owner entries; built-in packs are disjoint), but this ticket moved it onto the routine live replace path, and a dropped edge transitively breaks `executeRemove`'s "still-owned resource is never deleted" guarantee.

## LOW recorded, not fixed

(1) The replace bucket reports `retired: true` from plan-time `op.from`/`op.to` rather than the callee's returned metadata — a stale plan could announce a retire that didn't happen; unreachable via `reconcilePack`, but the `applyPlan` API permits it. (2) A framework-repo edge where the search path collapses to one entry yields an empty candidates list in the error — fail-safe, but ambiguous-empty against the Empty-result contract's spirit. (3) "No window in which the skill is absent" isn't literally true at the fs level — the pre-existing `rmSync`→`cpSync` window applies; self-heals on the next reconcile. (4) Test budget clean.

comments.author: orchestrator
comments.body:
**HUMAN RATIFICATION — MEDIUM-1 (production-inertness) is accepted as-is. No follow-up ticket.**

The review's MEDIUM-1 required an explicit human call: ratify that direction (a)'s retire rule never fires for any currently-reachable resource, or mint a follow-up giving `watch` an orderable pin so the rule bites.

**The human ratified the inertness.** Recording it so a future reader does not re-discover this as a defect.

**What is being ratified, precisely:**

- The planner acts on `kind: "skill"` only (`src/pack-reconcile.js:183-190`).
- The only skill-kind resources are `watch` (pin `83da59fa…`) and `ui-ux-pro-max` (pin `12b486b2…`), both git shas.
- `comparePinPrecedence` is decidable only for exact-semver pairs, so **both resolve to `'undecidable'`**.
- Therefore, for every resource this code can act on today, the outcome is **keep both copies and surface the ambiguity** — never auto-retire.
- The decidable "plugin wins" branch is real, tested, and exercised only by fixtures until a skill-kind resource carries an orderable pin.

**Why ratifying is the right call rather than changing the pin convention now:** nothing is broken. The behaviour is safe (never destructive), honest (a consumer is told the drift exists and cannot be ordered), and correctly documented in `docs/design/addon-packs.md` §2.4, `commands/design-pack.md` Step 4, and both `orchestrator-routing/SKILL.md` copies. Changing the pin format is a schema-and-migration decision affecting every existing lockfile, and it is a bigger design move than this ticket's premise supports — it would be adopting option (c)-shaped work under the banner of option (a).

**What this means operationally, and what a future reader should expect:** a `/watch` vs `/hivemind:watch` divergence remains a **manual-review event** for the foreseeable future. The reconcile report names it; a human decides. That is the accepted steady state, not an oversight.

**The condition that would change this:** the first skill-kind resource pinned to exact semver makes the decidable branch live for that resource. If that becomes common, revisit the pin convention deliberately — as its own ticket, with the migration cost priced in — rather than as a carry-forward.
